question:
RECOMMEND: APPROVE — advance to a revised spec, and answer the three open decisions in the same pass.

Why approve: your six annotations are folded in, the access blocker is CLEARED and proven (not assumed), and 2023 is confirmed by inspection rather than on your word. The scope is now grounded in what the source actually contains. Nothing here needs another ideation round.

DECISION EFFECT: approve advances 061 to spec, where an agent writes a revised specification against the real source and returns for a gate. Reject holds it at ideation with your feedback.

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY IT MATTERS: the source is not what this feature was built around. It is one tab, Daily (gid=1209807047), holding 2024, 2023 AND 2022 as three stacked 26-row bands, day-level with real dates. The taxonomy is 9 buckets over 17 sub-categories, not 25 over 61. There are no income rows and no aggregate rows — the aggregates are columns. Roughly 1,670 rows for both years, which kills the pagination worry outright.

THREE THINGS ONLY YOU CAN ANSWER:

(1) 2022 — in or out? New fact. The tab holds a full 2022 band alongside 2023 and 2024. This feature is titled and scoped to 2023-2024. Including 2022 is roughly a third more data from the same tab in the same shape, so it is cheap now and a separate feature later. Your call.

(2) D4 date granularity — your answer changed shape, not urgency. The source is day-level with real dates, so the old "date everything the 15th" option is no longer the best available; a real per-day date is. The remaining question is narrower: what to do with days the source cannot date — 16 damaged December 2024 columns and about 3 missing days in 2023. Drop them, park them on the month's last dated day, or fix them by hand in the normalization sheet.

(3) D3 undo, blast radius, and whether staging goes first. Uncontested and still unanswered. The verified constraint stands: load-local-env.js resolves SPREADSHEET_ID from functions/.env or the repo-root .env.local and never from functions/.env.staging, so no admin script can be aimed at staging today without a small change. If you want a staging rehearsal before production, that plumbing has to be built.

artifacts.summary:
SEED OUTCOME, UNCHANGED: the app itself holds your historical expense records, so those years are visible alongside day-to-day logging instead of living only in Google Sheets. Feasibility judged and reported before any write.

ACCESS — CLEARED, AND PROVEN. spreadsheets.get through expense-tracker-staging@expense-sheet-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com returns the workbook and all nine tabs. Two negative controls were run in the same probe: the Drive connector still returns "Requested entity was not found", and the PRODUCTION service account returns 403. The working route is specifically the staging account — which matters, because load-local-env.js resolves the production key.

2023 — CONFIRMED BY INSPECTION, not on the captain's word. Tab gid=1209807047 is titled Daily, 1061x749. Row 31 is a date-header row beginning "Jan 2023"; row 32 is the column-label row; rows 33-58 are 26 data rows. gid=0 turned out to be a P&L tab, not the source at all — every reference to it has been corrected.

WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY IS, versus what this entity previously assumed:
- One tab holding THREE stacked year bands: 2024 (rows 3-28), 2023 (33-58), 2022 (63-88). 2022 was not previously known to exist.
- Day-level matrix of item/amount column pairs with twelve month-total columns interleaved — NOT a monthly matrix.
- Taxonomy is 9 top-level buckets over 17 sub-categories — NOT 25 over 61.
- Column A holds two values tab-wide, not the four row-kind tags previously assumed.
- No income rows. No aggregate rows; the aggregates are columns.
- Rental property lives in a free-text detail column.
- Measured size: ~1,670 rows for 2023 and 2024 together. This is a measurement, not an estimate, and it retires the pagination concern.

TWO FINDINGS THAT LIMIT WHAT THE SPEC CAN PROMISE:
- December 2024's day headers are duplicated and truncated at 12-16, leaving 16 undated days.
- The workbook does not reconcile against itself: only about 88% of populated row-month cells match the sum of their own day cells, clustered in October in both years.
Together these make AC-2 (reconcile within 1%) UNFALSIFIABLE as written, and they are the concrete reason the captain's normalization sheet is the right approach — the source cannot serve as its own correctness oracle, so a human-reviewed intermediate is where those get settled.

THE NORMALIZATION SHEET — ACCEPTED, with its cost stated honestly. It does NOT replace the parser; it relocates the parser's output to a place the captain can correct. Net scope goes UP, not down, and it raises a new question the spec must answer: whether hand edits survive a re-generate.

CAPTAIN ANNOTATIONS A1-A6, ALL FOLDED: tab pointer corrected and 2023 confirmed (A1); categories answered — and gov_category turns out to need no mapping at all, since it is a Categories property and not an Expenses column (A2); rental/income answered by reading the 008/migrate-2025.js precedent and stating it concretely rather than copying "follow what we did for 2026" forward (A3); normalization sheet accepted with scope effect stated (A4); blocking precondition rewritten against the observed read (A5); personal-data context folded into Out of Scope and the risk section (A6).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA STATE: 14 criteria. AC-13 is satisfied here — the gid inspection happened. AC-2, AC-3 and AC-4 were written against premises now known false and are marked for recutting at spec. AC-14 is proposed to carry AC-13's gating role. Everything uncontested was preserved: the 051 precedent, the load-local-env blast-radius finding, AC-12, and AC-1/5/6/7/8/9/10/11.

REPRODUCIBILITY CAVEAT, stated by the agent unprompted: the five probe scripts live in the gitignored functions/backfill-reports/061-probe/ and need functions/.env.staging, so they are not runnable from a fresh clone. They print structure and counts only — no amounts, item names, or detail labels — deliberately, under AC-11, this being personal financial data in a public repository. Build should promote the extraction logic into a committed script with fixtures rather than depend on them.

CHECKLIST ACCOUNTING: 4 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed.
